newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on dollar inflows.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended slightly stronger at 26.223 to the dollar on Thursday from the previous day's close of 26.227, helped by the higher-than-expected dollar inflows for portfolio and direct equity investments, traders said.
"After resting on Wednesday, banks started selling again," said a foreign bank trader.
Volume was heavy at $132.48 million from $82.70 million.
As expected, the Central Bank came in to cap the peso's advance, traders said. They estimate it bought at least $30 million at 26.220 to 26.223 pesos.

"The Central bank had initially quoted a buy at 26.215. But it eventually took up dollars at 26.220 pesos and later at 26.223 pesos. It seems it didn't want the peso to go higher than 26.22 pesos," the same trader said.

Another trader said some banks took the opportunity to shore up their dollar positions due to expectations Treasury bill rates will again fall during the regular Monday auction next week. - LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841 8937
